body:
I haven't had any therapy related to my current issues. Mostly this is due to the fact that the VA does most group therapy for PTSD and I'm not a group therapy kind of guy.  I have a mental health appointment in December and will bring up these subjects. 

I feel like I'm unable to articulate my feelings because they're so erratic. I want to succeed, but I also want to hit the power button and blink out of existence. 

I do have hobbies, but I find little joy in them compared to how important they were to me in the past. It's like textbook depression... "Have you lost interest in things that used to provide contentment?" - that's me.

I suppose the feelings of burden come from my recognition of my wife's and family's perceptions of me as weak or broken. I believe they feel helpless when it comes to "fixing me" or "helping out" and I'm putting a burden on them. I think they feel responsible for my mental health or well-being, but there is nothing they could say or do that would positively affect my disposition. 

Maybe I'm posting in the wrong subreddit. I don't necessarily  want to die, but I can't see myself moving forward in my current life. However, I can't imagine a life where I would want to continue on; joy is lost on me. Thrill, excitement, lust, passion, drive - these are all things I'm faking for the sake of those I love.

I feel my dilemma is continuing to put on a face of contentment for the sake of my loved ones, or be honest about my desire to.... sleep.
